porbos.title: Trust in Allah, but Calculation Too • Ten Years, One Call • The Fire of Bu‘ath • Six, Then Twelve • Madinah’s First Teacher • Seventy-Three • The Terms of the Night of ‘Aqabah • The Shout of Shaytan • The Pursuit After ‘Aqabah • Hijrah, One by One • Umm Salamah’s Lone Journey

blocks.0: Trust in Allah, but Calculation Too
blocks.1: The season of Hajj. Rows of tents at Mina. A man is walking among the tents. This very man has travelled through the seven heavens. At Sidrat al-Muntaha he was summoned. Fifty to five. And coming down in the morning, he saw that Makkah was just as it had been.
blocks.2: The three-year siege had passed. Abu Talib was gone, Khadijah (RA) was gone. He had to return from Ta’if struck by stones.{{1}}
blocks.3: Yet he did not stop. The message of Allah is not a thing that stops. It must be delivered. And to deliver it, one needs a land where people will listen, and where one can stay safe with faith.
blocks.4: Today’s dars is the story of searching for that land; of searching for a home. A pledge in the dark of night in the mountain pass of ‘Aqabah. Then a night’s farewell, leaving Makkah. The cave on Mount Thawr. And finally, in a city of date orchards, a she-camel coming to a halt.
blocks.5: The reckoning of time is from the mouth of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA).
blocks.7: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} was sent (as a prophet) at the age of forty. After that he stayed in Makkah for thirteen years; revelation came to him. Then he was commanded to make the Hijrah.{{2}}
blocks.8: Today is the story of the final chapter of those thirteen years. One question will be with us through the whole story. Did the Prophet {{1}} sit relying only on Allah? Or at every step did he also calculate along with his trust?
blocks.9: And in our own work, how much is trust, and how much is calculation?
blocks.11: That search for a home the Prophet {{1}} did at market after market, fair after fair. At ‘Ukaz, at Majinnah, and in the Hajj season at Mina. Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA) has told of those days. He himself is a man of Yathrib; a man right at the heart of the events.
blocks.13: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stayed in Makkah ten years. Going to the people’s camping places, at ‘Ukaz and Majinnah and in the Hajj season at Mina, he would say, who will give me shelter? Who will help me, so that I may deliver the message of my Lord; and for that person, Paradise.{{2}}
blocks.16: It even happened that someone would come from Yemen or Egypt (the narrator said it so); his people would come and say, beware of the boy of Quraysh, lest he put you into trial. He would walk among their tents, and they would point at him with their fingers.{{1}}
blocks.17: Then one day the answer to that call came. It came from where no one expected.
blocks.19: Yathrib was then a weary city. Aws and Khazraj; two tribes of the same city. Long enmity. Blood for blood. And the most terrible of those wars was named Bu‘ath.{{1}}
blocks.20: ‘A’ishah (RA) has told of that day in one sentence.
blocks.22: The day of Bu‘ath was a day Allah had brought forward (in advance) for His Messenger. When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} came (to Madinah), their ranks had broken, their chiefs were killed, and many were wounded. In this way, concerning their entry into Islam, Allah had brought that day forward for His Messenger.{{2}}
blocks.23: A city had been shattered by war. In that shattered city, one day, a man was needed who could hold everyone together. Allah had made the very time of breaking into the preparation before the coming of His Prophet.
blocks.25: In one Hajj season the Prophet {{1}} met six men at Mina. All were of the Khazraj tribe. He spoke with them, called them to Allah. In Yathrib their neighbours were the Jews. Whenever a quarrel broke out, the Jews would say, the time of a prophet is near; we will go with him and kill you the way ‘Ad and Iram were killed. The six turned to one another and said, by Allah, this is the very prophet the Jews name to frighten us. Let them not reach him before us.{{2}}
blocks.26: They believed. And before leaving they said, our tribe is broken by war; there is no enmity like it in any other tribe. Perhaps Allah will join us together through you. We will go back and call them. If Allah gathers them around you, no one will be more honoured than you.
blocks.27: The six went back. The next Hajj, twelve came; ten of the Khazraj, two of the Aws. At the pass of ‘Aqabah they pledged at the hand of the Prophet {{1}}. This is the first ‘Aqabah.{{2}}
blocks.28: The terms of that pledge ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA) has told in his own words.
blocks.30: I am one of those naqibs who pledged to the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. We pledged on this: that we would not associate anything with Allah, would not steal, would not commit adultery, would not kill the soul Allah has made sacred, would not plunder, would not disobey; in return, Paradise, if we fulfilled these. And if we fell into any of these, the decision about it is in Allah’s hands.{{2}}
blocks.31: One thing needs to be clear here. In this narration of Bukhari it is not written which night of ‘Aqabah it is about. Ibn Ishaq called it the terms of the first ‘Aqabah; that part is from the Sirah, not in the main text of the hadith. The aim was one: tawhid and character. War had not yet come up.
blocks.33: As the twelve returned they left a request. Send with us someone who will teach us our din.{{1}}
blocks.34: The Prophet {{1}} sent Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA). A strange city. In hand only the Qur’an. What happened afterwards in house after house of Yathrib, Jabir (RA) has told himself.
blocks.36: At last Allah sent us from Yathrib to him. We gave him shelter, we affirmed him as true. One of us would go out, believe in him, and he would make him recite the Qur’an; he would return to his people, and they too would become Muslims through his Islam. In the end there remained no house among the Ansar in which a group of Muslims was not openly showing Islam.{{1}}
blocks.37: What was not found in ten years going door to door, Allah gave from a place whose name was then in no one’s calculation. No army, no sword; one teacher, and the Qur’an.
blocks.38: After faith came, the Muslims of Yathrib sat among themselves. A question on their lips.
blocks.40: We said, how long shall we leave the Messenger of Allah {{1}} like this? He is being chased from mountain to mountain of Makkah, and he lives in fear.{{2}}
blocks.41: That question they answered themselves; a caravan, on the road to Makkah.
blocks.43: The next Hajj. A caravan came from Yathrib to Makkah. In the caravan there were polytheists and Muslims. The Muslims kept their faith hidden. Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA) said, we were keeping the matter secret from the polytheists with us.{{1}}
blocks.44: They also decided not to leave without one man. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA); their chief. They said to him, you are one of our chiefs, one of our notable men. We cannot accept that tomorrow you will be fuel for Hell. He accepted Islam. He was present that night at ‘Aqabah. Later he also became a naqib (leader).{{1}}
blocks.45: When a third of the night had passed, they rose from their beds. Unknown to everyone. In the words of Ka‘b (RA), as quietly and stealthily as sandgrouse. Seventy-three men gathered in the pass. With them two women; Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA), whose kunyah is Umm ‘Umarah, and Asma’ bint ‘Amr (RA), who is also called Umm Mani‘.{{1}}
blocks.46: Another person also came to the pass whom no one had expected. The Prophet {{1}} came to the pass, with his uncle ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib. He was still in the religion of his tribe. But he wanted to see his nephew’s affair with his own eyes, to be certain. ‘Abbas spoke first of all. He said, O people of the Khazraj! You know what Muhammad is among us. Even from those who think as we do, we have protected him. He is honoured among his own tribe, safe in his own city. Yet he wishes to go to you. If you think you can keep the call by which you called him and protect him from his opponents, then take your responsibility. And if you think you will take him and abandon him, then stop right now.{{2}}
blocks.47: In reply they said, we have heard your words. O Messenger of Allah, now you speak. Take from us what you wish, for yourself and for your Lord.
blocks.48: The Terms of the Night of ‘Aqabah
blocks.49: The Prophet {{1}} recited the Qur’an. He called to Allah. Then he stated the terms. Jabir (RA) has kept the sentences of the terms by heart.
blocks.51: You will pledge to me to listen and obey, in times of eagerness and in times of laziness; to spend, in ease and in hardship; to command good and forbid evil; to speak for Allah, fearing no blame of any blamer in the matter of Allah; and when I come to you, you will help me and protect me as you protect yourselves, your wives and your children. And for you, Paradise.{{1}}
blocks.52: They stood up. They stretched out their hands. But before the hands touched, one stopped them. As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA); one of the youngest of the group.
blocks.54: Wait, people of Yathrib! We have driven our camels this far only because we know that this is the Messenger of Allah. To take him out today means to cut ties with all of Arabia, to see the best of you killed, and to be bitten by swords. If you can bear all this, take him; your reward is with Allah. And if you fear cowardice within yourselves, leave him now; with Allah that is the more acceptable excuse for you. They said, step aside, As‘ad (RA)! By Allah, we will never give up this pledge, never take it back.{{1}}
blocks.55: The smallest man said the most careful word. Then al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA) took the hand of the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.57: Yes, by Him who sent you with the truth, we will protect you from whatever we protect our izar (that is, our families) from. Take our pledge, O Messenger of Allah! We are children of war, men of arms; we have inherited this from our elders.{{1}}
blocks.58: In the midst of the talk another man cut in. Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA). A fear was in his mind. We are cutting all the old treaties with the Jews. If Allah gives you victory, will you go back to your own people and leave us? The Prophet {{1}} smiled. Then he said, blood is my blood, destruction is my destruction. I am yours, you are mine. Whoever you fight, I will fight; whoever you make peace with, I will make peace with.{{2}}
blocks.59: Then the matter of the naqibs.
blocks.61: Bring out to me twelve naqibs from among you, who will be in charge of their respective tribes. They brought out twelve naqibs; nine of the Khazraj, three of the Aws.{{1}}
blocks.62: Among the nine of the Khazraj were As‘ad ibn Zurarah, Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur, ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA). Among the three of the Aws was Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA).{{1}}
blocks.63: A small point; after ten years of rejection, those who came and stood beside the Prophet {{1}} were also willing to take responsibility for their own tribes. The pledge was not only in emotion; it was in structure too.
blocks.65: The pledge ended. Just then a shout rose from the top of ‘Aqabah.
blocks.67: When we finished the pledge, Shaytan shouted from the top of ‘Aqabah in a voice so far-reaching that I had never heard the like; O people of the camps! Have you nothing to do about Mudhammam and the apostates with him? (Ibn Ishaq explained: the enemy of Allah meant Muhammad by this.) They have agreed to war against you! The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, this is the ‘Azab of ‘Aqabah, the son of Azyab (that is, Shaytan). Listen, enemy of Allah! By Allah, I will surely make time for you. Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, go back to your tents. ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) said, by Him who sent you with the truth, if you wish, tomorrow we will fall upon the people of Mina with our swords. The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, I have not been commanded to do this.{{4}}
blocks.68: At dawn the elders of Quraysh arrived. Right at the tents of the Yathrib caravan, one after another. They said, O people of the Khazraj! We have heard that you came to our companion. You want to take him out from among us, and you pledged at his hand for war against us. By Allah, there is no tribe among the Arabs with whom a war breaking out with us is more disliked by us than with you. Then the polytheists of the caravan swore by Allah and said, nothing like this happened, we know nothing. And they spoke the truth; they truly did not know. The Muslims kept looking at one another’s faces.{{1}}
blocks.69: The Quraysh group was getting up to leave. Among them a youth of the Makhzum tribe, with shiny new shoes on his feet. Ka‘b (RA) said in passing, Abu Jabir, can you not get a pair of shoes like this Qurayshi youth? Hearing it, the youth took off his shoes and threw them at him. He said, by Allah, you will wear these. In a night full of fear there was such a small light moment too.{{1}}
blocks.71: Quraysh went back, but suspicion did not. They went to ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul; the greatest chief of the Khazraj. They said the same thing: your people have reportedly pledged for war with our companion. He said, this is a great matter. My tribe would not do this without informing me; I know nothing. They went back.{{1}}
blocks.72: Mina began to empty. Quraysh enquired and learned the event was true. They set out after the caravan. Two naqibs were caught; Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA). Mundhir broke away and escaped. They caught Sa‘d (RA). They tied his hand to his neck with the camel’s rope. Beating him, dragging him by the hair, they brought him into Makkah.
blocks.73: While I was in their hands, some of the Quraysh came. Among them a fair, handsome man. I said to myself, if any of these has anything good, it will be with this one. He came close, raised his hand, and punched me hard. Then I knew that these have nothing good left.{{1}}
blocks.74: Then one of them said, do you not have a security pact with anyone of Quraysh? Sa‘d (RA) said, I do. I used to give security to the trade caravan of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im in my area, so that no one would wrong them. And the caravan of al-Harith ibn Harb too. The man said, then call out the names of those two. He called. Those two were sitting in the mosque beside the Ka‘bah then. Hearing the news they said, he speaks the truth; he used to give our traders security and did not let wrong be done to them. They came and freed Sa‘d (RA).{{1}}
blocks.76: Allah showed the Prophet {{1}} the home. In a dream. In the narration of Suhayb (RA) the Prophet {{2}} had said it was either Hajar or Yathrib.{{3}}
blocks.78: The Prophet {{1}} was then in Makkah. He said to the Muslims, I have been shown the home of your Hijrah; full of date palms, between two stony lands (harrah). So those who were to go made Hijrah toward Madinah; and most of those who had made Hijrah to Abyssinia also returned to Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.79: Then from Makkah, on the road to Madinah, people began to leave one or two at a time. Who arrived first, al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) has told.
blocks.81: The first to come to us were Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum (RA); they would teach the people the Qur’an. Then came Bilal, Sa‘d and ‘Ammar ibn Yasir (RA). Then ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) came with twenty of the Companions of the Prophet {{1}}. Then the Prophet {{2}} came. I never saw the people of Madinah as happy about anything as they were at the arrival of the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Even the slave girls were saying, the Messenger of Allah {{4}} has come! Before he came I had already recited several surahs of the Mufassal, including ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’.{{5}}
blocks.82: Madinah was filling up. But not everyone’s road was easy. The Prophet {{1}} used to tell the travellers one thing; Allah has arranged for you brothers and a home where you will be safe.{{2}}
blocks.84: Among the Muhajirun of Makkah, the first to set out on the road to Madinah was Abu Salamah (RA). About a year before the pledge of ‘Aqabah.{{1}}
blocks.85: He seated his wife Umm Salamah (RA) and their infant son Salamah on the camel. He himself took the reins. Umm Salamah (RA) later told in her own words what happened.
blocks.86: When Abu Salamah (RA) set out leading me by the camel’s reins, the men of Banu Mughirah stood before him. They said, you have been lost to us as regards yourself. But on what assurance will you take this daughter of ours around from town to town? They snatched the reins from his hand and tore me away. Then Banu ‘Abd al-Asad, the tribe of Abu Salamah (RA), grew angry. They said, by Allah, we will not leave our boy with her. They pulled at my son Salamah until even his hand was dislocated. Then Banu ‘Abd al-Asad took him away, and Banu Mughirah kept me back. Abu Salamah (RA) went on to Madinah. Between me and my son and husband a separation came.{{1}}
blocks.87: Every morning I would go out and sit at al-Abtah. I would weep until evening. So for a year, or close to it.{{1}}
blocks.88: One day a cousin from Banu Mughirah was passing that way. Pity came over him. He said to the tribesmen, why are you not letting this helpless girl go? You separated her from her husband, and from her son too. They said, go, go to your husband, if you wish. Banu ‘Abd al-Asad also gave the boy back. Umm Salamah (RA) set out on a camel, seating her son on her lap. No one else with her. Only Allah, and the boy. At a place named Tan‘im she met ‘Uthman ibn Talhah. He was still a polytheist. He asked, where are you going? Umm Salamah (RA) said, to Madinah, to my husband. He said, no one is with you? The answer came, no one but Allah and this boy. ‘Uthman ibn Talhah said, by Allah, you cannot be left alone. He took the camel’s reins and walked.
blocks.89: By Allah, I never found a gentler companion than him among any man of the Arabs. Wherever we stopped, he would make the camel kneel and step aside. When I got down, he would unload the camel and tie it to a tree, then go away and lie down under a tree. When it was time to set out, he would bring the camel forward, saddle it, and step back, saying, mount. When I had settled properly, he would come and take the reins. In this way he brought me to Madinah. When the settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf at Quba came into view, he said, your husband is in that village. Enter with Allah’s blessing. Then he turned back toward Makkah.{{1}}
blocks.90: Umm Salamah (RA) would later say, no household in Islam suffered such hardship as the family of Abu Salamah (RA).

The same incident is also in al-Raheeq al-Makhtum (Allamah Safiur Rahman Mubarakpuri, p. 272; citing Ibn Hisham and Zad al-Ma‘ad as sources).

In this narration doubt about the name of the place is reported.

The account from the witness’s own mouth, with connected chain; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene. It is also in al-Raheeq al-Makhtum, pp. 273–274.

quiz.q: In the narration of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), how many years did the Prophet ﷺ stay in Makkah after receiving prophethood?
o: Thirteen years
Ten years, as long as he went around calling at the markets
Fourteen nights, as long as he stayed at Quba
Three nights, as long as he hid in the cave of Thawr
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3902 and 3851: for thirteen years in Makkah revelation came; then the command of Hijrah.

quiz.q: Someone does not calculate in business, saying ‘Allah is my trust’. With which scene of the Hijrah can he be made to understand?
o: Sitting only three nights in the cave, with the spider’s web, and getting results with no arrangement at all
After four months of preparation and a guide, saying in the cave ‘Allah is with us’
Suhayb (RA) gaining release by giving gold, where the arrangement was only the giving of gold
Building a mosque where the she-camel knelt, where no price had to be paid
quiz.e: The answer to today’s question: trust and calculation together.

quiz.q: In the narration of Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA), at which places did the Prophet ﷺ go to the people in search of a home?
o: The pass of ‘Aqabah, the cave of Thawr and Quba
‘Ukaz and Majinnah, and in the Hajj season at Mina
The harrah, the settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf and the date-drying yard of the mosque
The settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf and the courtyard of Abu Ayyub (RA)

quiz.q: In the Hajj season the Prophet ﷺ would say, ‘Who will give me shelter? Who will help me?’ What was the promise in return?
o: A reward equal to the blood-price, which Quraysh had announced
A written paper of security, which was written for Suraqah
Paradise
The glad tidings of a ‘profitable trade’, which were given to Suhayb (RA)

quiz.q: What is said about the day of Bu‘ath in the narration of ‘A’ishah (RA)?
o: On that day the Prophet ﷺ came to the house of Abu Bakr (RA) at the harsh time of noon
On that day al-Zubayr (RA) met the Muslim caravan returning from Syria
On that day seventy-three men gathered in the pass of ‘Aqabah
Allah had brought that day forward for His Messenger

quiz.q: How did the war of Bu‘ath make easier the way for Islam to come?
o: The Jews had promised to protect the Muslims, in this hope
Quraysh had stopped looking toward Madinah, in this hope
With the tribes’ ranks broken and the chiefs killed, the way became easier
‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib had made a pact with Yathrib, in this hope
quiz.e: According to the narration of ‘A’ishah (RA) (Sahih al-Bukhari 3777).

quiz.q: According to Ibn Ishaq’s narration, to which tribe did the first six who met the Prophet ﷺ belong?
o: Khazraj
Aws, with whom the Khazraj used to fight
Quraysh, who lived in Makkah
Banu Dil, one of whom became a guide

quiz.q: Why did the six not delay in believing?
o: Hearing the promise of Paradise in the terms of ‘Aqabah, which was an event of the second ‘Aqabah
Thinking, this is the very prophet the Jews threatened them with
Hearing the warning of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, which was an event of the second ‘Aqabah
Seeing the sign of the she-camel kneeling, which happened in Madinah
quiz.e: The words of the six: this is the very prophet; let them not reach him before us (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: How many came at the first ‘Aqabah pledge?
o: Seventy-three, who were at the second ‘Aqabah
Six, who were at the first meeting
Twelve
Seventy, the number in the hadith of Jabir (RA)
quiz.e: Ten of the Khazraj and two of the Aws (Ibn Ishaq).

quiz.q: Which is the term of the pledge narrated by ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA)?
o: Choosing twelve naqibs and taking responsibility for the tribes, which happened at the second ‘Aqabah
Protecting me as you protect your wives and children, which was a term of the second ‘Aqabah
Whoever you make peace with, I will make peace with, which was said to Abu al-Haytham
Abstaining from shirk, theft, adultery, unjust killing and plunder

quiz.q: According to Ibn Ishaq’s account, the pledge of the first ‘Aqabah was from what time?
o: After hiding in the cave of Thawr
The time of staying fourteen nights at Quba
After Suraqah went back
Before war was made obligatory
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq: like the pledge of the women, before war was made obligatory (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: In the narration of Jabir (RA), how did Islam spread in Yathrib?
o: Hearing of the Jews’ threats, all the tribes believed together
One would believe and, having learned the Qur’an, return, and his people too would become Muslims
After the war of Bu‘ath the tribes united, then everyone believed
Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) came and in a single day called everyone and made them Muslims

quiz.q: What lesson does the dars attach to Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr’s (RA) going to Madinah?
o: The ground was prepared by a teacher, not an army
Gathering in the dark of the night at the pass of ‘Aqabah was the real work
Going back, unable to catch him, was Suraqah’s real victory
The kneeling of the she-camel was the real preparation
quiz.e: Mus‘ab (RA) went first; then the Prophet ﷺ; by then the home was ready.

quiz.q: Your child wants to learn the din from someone. What can be learned from the story of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) in Madinah?
o: Only the preparation of swords is the real thing
To teach everything oneself, without sending a teacher
A capable teacher builds the home
A secret caravan is needed to teach the din

quiz.q: In the narration of Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA), how many men and how many women were there on the night of the second ‘Aqabah?
o: Twelve men and two women, the number of the first ‘Aqabah
Seventy men and one woman, the narration of ‘Urwah
Seventy-three men and two women
Six men, no woman, the number of the first meeting
quiz.e: In the narration of ‘Urwah and Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, seventy and one (Ibn Kathir).

quiz.q: Who were the two women Companions present at the second ‘Aqabah?
o: ‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr (RA) and Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA)
Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA) and Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA)
Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA) and ‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr (RA)
Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA) and Asma’ bint ‘Amr (RA)
quiz.e: Al-Bidayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’.

quiz.q: Who spoke first of all on the night of ‘Aqabah?
o: His uncle ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib
The youngest, As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA)
The chief al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA), who first took his hand
Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA), who raised the question of the pact
quiz.e: First of all, the word of his uncle ‘Abbas (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: Your friend has known the truth for many years and still does not believe. What can be learned from the story of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA)?
o: No need to speak once the friend understands by himself; he will come on his own
It is enough to make the friend memorise the terms of ‘Aqabah; the rest is his work
Winning an argument in front of Quraysh, silencing him and turning him back
Speaking with love: ‘You will be fuel for Hell; I cannot accept it’
quiz.e: Al-Bidayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’.

quiz.q: What did As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA) warn of before the pledge?
o: We are cutting the old pacts; will the Prophet ﷺ go back? (the question of Abu al-Haytham)
Taking the Prophet ﷺ out means a break with all of Arabia
Tomorrow we will fall upon the people of Mina with our swords (the proposal of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA))
We are children of war, we inherited arms (the words of al-Bara’ (RA))

quiz.q: In answer to the question of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: I have not been commanded to do this, which was said to ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA)
What do you think of two of whom the third is Allah? which was said to Abu Bakr (RA)
I am yours, you are mine
In exchange for a price, which was said when taking Abu Bakr’s (RA) mount

quiz.q: At the second ‘Aqabah, what were the number and division of the naqibs the Prophet ﷺ asked for?
o: Twelve; ten of the Khazraj, two of the Aws
Six; all of the Khazraj
Seventy-three; among them two women
Twelve; nine of the Khazraj, three of the Aws

quiz.q: What is understood from the warning of As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA)?
o: The pledge was kept hidden because no one was willing to take the risk
The risk was told openly to everyone before the pledge
The Prophet ﷺ himself objected to taking the pledge
Quraysh already knew all the terms of the pledge

quiz.q: Hearing the shout from ‘Aqabah, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: This is the ‘Azab of ‘Aqabah, the son of Azyab; I will make time for you
Mount in safety and be followed, which the Ansar said at the harrah
Keep our matter secret, which was said to Suraqah
Go slowly; I hope I will be permitted too, which was said to Abu Bakr (RA)

quiz.q: What did ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) propose to the Prophet ﷺ?
o: To deny everything by oath before Quraysh, like the polytheists of the caravan
To fall upon the people of Mina with swords the very next day
To take one of two mounts, like Abu Bakr (RA)
To donate the yard, like the two boys
quiz.e: Answer: ‘I have not been commanded to do this’ (Musnad Ahmad 15798).

quiz.q: What did Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA) say about the oath of the polytheists of the caravan?
o: They swore falsely, pretending though they knew everything
They spoke out of fear of the Muslims, though they knew the real matter
They spoke the truth; they did not know
They spoke on the order of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA), knowing it

quiz.q: Which naqib was caught by Quraysh after ‘Aqabah?
o: Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA), who broke away and escaped
Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA)
As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA), who had stopped them before the pledge
Al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA), who first took his hand

quiz.q: How was Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) released?
o: By agreeing to give gold, like Suhayb (RA)
By changing beds, like ‘Ali (RA)
By mentioning the security he had given to two merchants of Quraysh
Through the intercession of ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy
quiz.e: By calling out the names of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im and al-Harith ibn Harb (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: A trader does not value small good conduct. What can be said from the story of Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA)?
o: By conduct, people’s loyalty can be bought
An opportunity is created for the enemy to ask forgiveness
The profit of business only keeps increasing
In the future it can save life in danger
quiz.e: The two merchants to whom he had given security were the ones who freed him.

quiz.q: Who first came to Madinah and began to teach people the Qur’an?
o: Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) and Ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
Bilal (RA) and ‘Ammar ibn Yasir (RA), who came after
‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and the twenty with him
As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA) and ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA), who were people of Madinah itself

quiz.q: Which statement did al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) make about himself?
o: He held a cloth and shaded the Prophet ﷺ from the sun at Quba, which was the act of Abu Bakr (RA)
Before the Prophet ﷺ came he had already recited several surahs of the Mufassal
He held his hand and stopped everyone before the pledge, which was the act of As‘ad (RA)
He slept in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed that night, which was the act of ‘Ali (RA)

quiz.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ see the home of the Hijrah in the dream (Sahih al-Bukhari 3905)?
o: At the foot of Mount Thawr, between two caves
Beside a high fortress, in the Jewish settlement
Full of date palms, between two harrahs
Beside the pass of ‘Aqabah, within the tents of Mina

quiz.q: Who escorted Umm Salamah (RA) on the road to Madinah?
o: Abu Salamah (RA), who had reached Madinah earlier
‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, who brought news to the cave
‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), who grazed the sheep
‘Uthman ibn Talhah, still a polytheist
quiz.e: Met at Tan‘im; up to Quba (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: Someone finds it hard to walk the path of din under family pressure. What can be learned from the story of Umm Salamah (RA)?
o: Leaving a business when it makes a loss, for the same reason
Trusting without opening the books before an exam, for the same reason
Bearing separation and weeping with patience, the way opens
Leaving a trust with someone, for the same reason

porbos.title: The Empty House of Banu Jahsh • ‘Ayyash’s Mother’s Oath • Waiting for Permission • The Night Council of Quraysh • The Visitor at Noon • The Bed of That Night • The Waistband of Asma’ • The Cave of Thawr • The Rock at Noon

blocks.0: The Empty House of Banu Jahsh
blocks.1: One day in a neighbourhood of Makkah an entire house became empty. ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh (RA) had gone with everyone of the household; his wife, his brothers, his sisters, women and men, all. Not a lock on the door; there was simply no one in the house. ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, ‘Abbas and Abu Jahl were passing by. ‘Utbah saw the doors of Banu Jahsh rattling in the wind. No one inside. He sighed. He said, every house, however long its happiness, one day calamity and misfortune seize it. The house of Banu Jahsh lies today without its people. Abu Jahl said, are you weeping for so-and-so’s son? Then he said to ‘Abbas, this is the work of your nephew. He has split our community, torn our affairs apart, caused separation among us.{{1}}
blocks.3: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) himself told how their Hijrah happened. Three decided: ‘Umar (RA), ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah (RA) and Hisham ibn al-‘As (RA). They would meet at dawn at a place called Tanadib outside Makkah. Whoever did not reach there, it would be understood that he had been held back; the other two would go on. ‘Umar (RA) and ‘Ayyash (RA) arrived. Hisham was held back; he fell into trial. Reaching Madinah they stayed at Quba. After some days Abu Jahl and his brother al-Harith came from Makkah. ‘Ayyash (RA) was their cousin, and on the mother’s side also a brother.
blocks.4: They said to ‘Ayyash (RA), your mother has vowed that no comb will touch her head until she sees you, and that she will not go from the sun into shade. ‘Ayyash’s (RA) heart softened. I said, by Allah, these people want to turn you away from your din; beware. If lice trouble your mother she will comb for herself; if the heat of Makkah grows she will go into shade.{{1}}
blocks.5: ‘Ayyash (RA) said, let me fulfil my mother’s oath. I also have some wealth in Makkah; I will bring it. ‘Umar (RA) said, I am one of the richest of Quraysh. Take half my wealth, do not go with them. ‘Ayyash (RA) did not listen. Then ‘Umar (RA) said, if you will go anyway, take this she-camel of mine. The she-camel is clever, fast. If you suspect anything of their intentions, flee on her back. After going some distance Abu Jahl said, brother, my camel is giving me much trouble. Will you let me ride a little on this she-camel of yours? ‘Ayyash (RA) said, of course. He made the camel kneel. He got down. As soon as the foot touched the ground, the two pounced and bound him. They brought him into Makkah and put him into trial. The mother’s oath was a ruse to bring the son back.
blocks.7: But the Prophet {{1}} did not go.
blocks.9: Abu Bakr (RA) prepared to go toward Madinah. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said to him, take it slowly; I hope I too will be given permission. Abu Bakr (RA) said, may my father be your ransom, do you hope for that? He said, yes. Then Abu Bakr (RA) held himself back to be a companion of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, and fed two mounts he had, for four months, the leaves of the samur tree.{{3}}
blocks.10: Four months. One man looking after two camels, only waiting for a single day. At ‘Aqabah Madinah had called him. But until the word ‘go’ came from Allah’s side, he did not lift his foot.
blocks.12: Meanwhile in Makkah Quraysh had sensed it. Islam was spreading fast. Many people in Madinah had believed. The companions of the Prophet {{1}} were leaving one by one.{{2}}
blocks.13: So they sat in consultation. The Qur’an itself tells of that night.
blocks.15: (O Prophet!) Remember the time when the disbelievers were plotting to imprison you or to kill you or to expel you (from the land). They were scheming, and Allah was also employing His plan. In truth, Allah is the best of planners.{{1}}
blocks.16: A little more detail of that night has been given by Ibn ‘Abbas (RA).
blocks.18: Quraysh consulted one night in Makkah. One of them said, when it is morning, bind him; they meant the Prophet {{1}}. Another said, rather kill him. Another said, rather expel him. Then Allah informed His Prophet of it.{{2}}
blocks.19: But the last sentence of the verse says whose hand holds the last move. What happened inside the council, Ibn Ishaq has told from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). Dar al-Nadwah; that house of Qusayy ibn Kilab, where Quraysh never rose without taking some great decision. At the door an old man. In a thick cloak. He said, I am a shaykh of Najd. I have heard what you have gathered about. My counsel may be of use. He was allowed in. In the narration, this shaykh was Iblis.{{1}}
blocks.20: In the council were ‘Utbah and Shaybah, Abu Sufyan, Jubayr ibn Mut‘im, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu al-Bakhtari, Hakim ibn Hizam, Abu Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and many others. One said, bind him in chains and keep him imprisoned in a house. He will die just as the poets before him died. The shaykh of Najd said, no. His word will surely get out from beyond this door. His companions will come and snatch him away. Another said, expel him from the city. The shaykh said, no. Have you not seen his sweet speech? He will go to any tribe of the Arabs, conquer them, and come back; what then? Then Abu Jahl said, I have an opinion that has not come to your minds. From every tribe one young man, spirited, of good lineage. In each one’s hand a sharp sword. All at once, one blow. Then his blood will be divided over all the tribes. Banu ‘Abd Manaf will not be able to fight everyone; they will agree to take blood-money, and we will pay it. The shaykh of Najd said, this man’s opinion is right. There is no other view than this. The council broke up.
blocks.22: That day ‘A’ishah (RA) was at home. Later she herself narrated it. Every day the Prophet {{1}} would come to the house of Abu Bakr (RA); once in the morning, once in the evening.{{2}}
blocks.23: That day he came at noon.
blocks.25: One day we were sitting in the house of Abu Bakr (RA), at the harsh time of noon. Someone said to Abu Bakr (RA), here is the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, coming with his head covered; at a time when he did not come to us. Abu Bakr (RA) said, may my father and mother be his ransom; by Allah, at this hour he must have come on some great matter.{{2}}
blocks.26: What the Prophet {{1}} said on entering reached the ears of ‘A’ishah (RA).
blocks.28: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} came, asked permission; permission was given, he entered. He said to Abu Bakr (RA), send out those who are with you. Abu Bakr (RA) said, they are only your family, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah. He said, I have been given permission to leave. Abu Bakr (RA) said, companionship? May my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, yes. Abu Bakr (RA) said, then take one of these two mounts of mine, may my father be your ransom. The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, for the price.{{4}}
blocks.29: ‘Companionship?’ One word. And an answer in one word, ‘Yes.’ Four months of waiting ended in one word.
blocks.31: The night of departure. The youths of Quraysh have surrounded the house of the Prophet {{1}}. The plan: in the morning all together to pounce.
blocks.33: That night ‘Ali (RA) spent the night in the bed of the Prophet {{1}}, and the Prophet {{2}} went out and reached the cave. The polytheists guarded ‘Ali (RA), thinking him the Prophet. In the morning they pounced on him; seeing ‘Ali (RA), Allah foiled their plot. They said, where is that companion of yours? He said, I do not know.{{3}}
blocks.34: The Prophet {{1}} did not say to anyone, come, let us flee. He left one man lying in the bed. And that ‘one’ lay there without a question.{{2}}
blocks.35: After the council broke up Jibril (AS) came and said to the Prophet {{1}}, tonight do not stay in your usual bed. Night came. The youths gathered at the door, to pounce as soon as the Prophet {{2}} slept. The Prophet {{3}} said to ‘Ali (RA), wear this green Hadrami cloak of mine and lie in my bed; no harm from them will reach you. He used to sleep wearing this very cloak.{{4}}
blocks.36: The scene after this has come with a still weaker chain. Ibn Ishaq took it from Muhammad ibn Ka‘b al-Qurazi, a Tabi‘i; in the chain is a narrator named Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, whom the hadith scholars have called weak. So this is only a scene. In the narration, before the people gathered at the door Abu Jahl was saying loudly, Muhammad says, if you follow his path you will be kings of the Arabs and non-Arabs, will be raised after death, will get Paradise; if you do not accept, you will be slaughtered, will be raised after death and burn in fire. Then the Prophet {{1}} came out. A handful of dust in his hand. He said, yes, I say that. And you are one of them. Allah took away their sight. The Prophet {{2}} went on reciting the opening verses of Surah Ya Sin as he scattered dust on their heads. One came and asked, whom are you waiting for here? They said, Muhammad. He said, may Allah thwart you. Muhammad has gone out putting dust on all your heads. Put a hand on your head and see. Each put a hand on his head. Dust. They peeked in and saw someone lying in the bed wrapped in a cloak. They said, there is Muhammad, sleeping. Morning came. From the bed rose ‘Ali (RA).{{3}}
blocks.38: Preparation for the journey was in the house of Abu Bakr (RA).
blocks.40: We prepared provisions for them swiftly, and packed food in a pouch. Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA) cut a piece of her waistband and tied the mouth of the pouch with it. For this reason she was named ‘Dhat al-Nitaq’ (the one with the waistband).{{1}}
blocks.41: In the arrangement of this journey everyone had one task.
blocks.43: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} and Abu Bakr (RA) reached a cave on Mount Thawr and hid there three nights. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr (RA) would spend the night with them; he was young, intelligent and sharp. In the last part of the night he would leave them, and in the morning be with Quraysh in Makkah, as if he had spent the night there. If he heard of any plot against them he would remember it, and when the darkness of evening fell he would come to them and tell. ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), the freed slave of Abu Bakr (RA), would graze a flock of milch goats for them, and after the first watch of the night had passed he would bring it to them. The two of them would spend the night on the milk of those goats and bread baked on hot stones.{{2}}
blocks.46: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} and Abu Bakr (RA) hired a man of the Banu Dil tribe as a guide; he was especially skilled at knowing the way. He was still in the religion of the disbelievers of Quraysh. Considering him trustworthy, they handed him their two mounts and took his promise that after three nights, at morning, he would arrive at the cave of Thawr with the mounts.{{2}}
blocks.47: In this choice the question was not of faith; it was of competence for the task and of trustworthiness. The right man for the right task. No one’s task is big, no one’s task is small; all tasks together make one journey.
blocks.49: Morning came. Makkah woke up. The one they were to catch was not in the bed. ‘Ali (RA) was there. Then the search began. House by house, road by road. A reward was announced. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) has said, they went on following the footprints.
blocks.51: They followed his footprints. Reaching the mountain the tracks became confused. They climbed the mountain, passed by the front of the cave, saw a spider’s web at its mouth. They said, had anyone entered here, the spider’s web would not be on its mouth. He stayed there three nights.{{1}}
blocks.54: In the cave I said to the Prophet {{1}}, if any of them looks beneath his feet, he will see us. He said, O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two of whom the third is Allah?{{2}}
blocks.55: In one sentence all the fear of the cave was washed away. The Qur’an has kept this event. The disbelievers had driven him out; he was ‘the second of the two’.
blocks.57: If you do not help him (that is, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace), (there is no harm to him in that. For) Allah did help him at that time too, when the disbelievers had driven him out (of Makkah), and he was the second of the two, when the two were in the cave, when he said to his companion, do not grieve, Allah is with us. So Allah sent down tranquillity upon him from Himself and helped him with forces you did not see, and made the word of the disbelievers the lowest. In truth the word of Allah is the highest. Allah is Mighty and Wise.{{1}}
blocks.58: Before the cave were four months of feeding camels, leaving someone in the bed, hiring a guide, having news brought at night. And inside the cave exactly this sentence. Preparation and trust; both together. The question with which today’s dars began, its answer is here.
blocks.60: After three nights he came out of the cave. They took the road, with the guide of Banu Dil, toward Madinah. About the road Abu Bakr (RA) himself has told. The father of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) was buying a camel-saddle from him; the father said, the saddle will not go until you tell the story of setting out from Makkah.
blocks.62: We set out from Makkah; we travelled the whole night and the whole day. The harsh time of noon came. I looked around to see if there was a little shade to take shelter in. I saw a rock. Going to it I saw that a little shade was there. I levelled the place and spread a bed for the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. I said, lie down, O Prophet of Allah. He lay down. I went out looking around to see whether anyone had followed. I saw a shepherd coming with his sheep toward that rock, wanting what we had wanted. I asked, O boy, whose are you? He named a man of Quraysh, and I recognised him. I said, is there milk in your sheep? He said, there is. I said, will you milk? He said, yes. I said, hold one sheep, brush the udder free of dust, then brush your hands. He struck one hand against the other to show. Then he milked some milk for me. I had a vessel for the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, with cloth wrapped around its mouth. I poured water over the milk so that the bottom cooled. Then I took it to the Prophet {{3}}. I saw that he had woken up. I said, drink, O Messenger of Allah. He drank so that my heart was filled with joy. Then I said, the time to travel has come. He said, yes. We set out.{{4}}
blocks.63: The Prophet {{1}} sleeping. And one man awake, guarding. First water in the vessel of milk, so that the hot milk would cool for the Prophet {{2}}. Another story of another place Abu Bakr (RA) has also told. In one tent, only a woman. She said, I am alone, go to the elders of the tribe. The Prophet {{3}} had set out toward that very tent. The woman’s son brought a thin goat. The Prophet {{4}} stroked its udder and milked; the vessel filled. That woman, then Abu Bakr (RA), then the other goats too; one by one everyone drank. The woman later used to call him ‘al-Mubarak’. Her goats multiplied. Abu Bakr (RA) later recognised that son in Madinah and said, this is the companion of that ‘al-Mubarak’. The woman came and said, take me to him. She went to the Prophet {{5}}, and the Prophet {{6}} gave her something.{{7}}

The verse ‘Utbah recited, according to Ibn Hisham, is from a poem of Abu Dawud al-Ayadi. At that time ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib had not believed.

footnotes.3: The background of the Quraysh council: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, note 18 on Surah al-Anfal 8:30, p. 496: when the disbelievers of Makkah saw that Islam was spreading fast and that many people in Madinah had accepted Islam, they called a consultative council. Three proposals came there: arrest, killing and exile. The final decision was that they would kill, choosing one youth from each of the various tribes and attacking together.
footnotes.4: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Anfal 8:30, p. 496 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.5: Musnad Ahmad 3251 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar: chain hasan
footnotes.6: The council of Dar al-Nadwah: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the reason for the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} himself’ (Ibn Ishaq ← ‘man la attahimu’ (an unspecified trustworthy person) ← Ibn Abi Najih ← Mujahid ← Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)). In the chain Ibn Ishaq did not disclose one person’s name; Ibn Kathir has said that al-Waqidi too has brought a similar account via ‘A’ishah, Ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Ali and Suraqah. footnotes.7: The Prophet’s {{1}} coming to the house of Abu Bakr (RA) every morning and evening: Sahih al-Bukhari 3905 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); the opening part of the hadith: ‘lam yamurra ‘alayna yawmun illa yatina fihi Rasulullahi {{2}} tarafayin nahari bukratan wa ‘ashiyyah’).
footnotes.10: Musnad Ahmad 3251 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar: chain hasan
footnotes.11: The matter of surrounding the house: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, note 18 on Surah al-Anfal 8:30, p. 496 (the enemies had besieged his house); in Musnad Ahmad 3251 too there is the polytheists’ guarding of ‘Ali (RA).

quiz.q: What did ‘Utbah do on seeing the empty house of Banu Jahsh?
o: Sighed and said, every house is seized by calamity one day
Blamed the Prophet ﷺ like Abu Jahl, then spoke to ‘Abbas
Took the house with ‘Abbas, then locked it
Sent men to bring back ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh (RA), then went back

quiz.q: What did ‘Umar (RA) offer ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah (RA) so that he would not go?
o: His own she-camel, which he gave at the time of going
Security of staying at Quba, which was for Abu Salamah (RA)
A pact with Abu Jahl, which never happened
Half of his own wealth

quiz.q: For how long did Abu Bakr (RA), hoping to be the Prophet’s ﷺ companion, feed his two mounts samur leaves?
o: Three nights, as long as they had to stay in the cave
Fourteen nights, as long as he stayed at Quba
Ten years, as long as he was called season after season
Four months

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ not go before the permission for Hijrah came?
o: He did not want to leave Makkah, so he sent his companions first
Abu Bakr’s (RA) mounts were not ready, so there was delay
The Ansar had not yet pledged, so he waited
He was waiting for Allah’s permission; the companions went first
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3905: ‘I hope I will be given permission’.

quiz.q: What is the last word of verse 8:30 about the night council of Quraysh?
o: They were plotting; Allah was also planning, He is the best of planners
Do not grieve, Allah is with us, which was said in the cave
The word of Allah is uppermost; Allah is Mighty and Wise, the words of 9:40
Allah sent down tranquillity upon him and sent unseen forces
quiz.e: Surah al-Anfal 8:30; the other three are the words of Surah al-Tawbah 9:40.

quiz.q: What was the main feature of the arrangement of the journey to the cave of Thawr?
o: Everyone staying together in the cave
Fixing one person for each task
Leaving it to supplication alone, with no preparation
Taking all help from the polytheists

quiz.q: The guide was a polytheist; why did the Prophet ﷺ still hire him?
o: He had secretly accepted Islam, so the Prophet ﷺ trusted him
Quraysh did not want to catch him, so it seemed safe
Because he was skilled at knowing the way and trustworthy
He was a relative of Abu Bakr (RA), so he was trusted

quiz.q: At work you have been given the responsibility of a task, one step of which you will give to another trustworthy person. Which scene matches?
o: Giving the guide’s task to one who was trustworthy and skilled
Giving someone responsibility because he is a relative of Abu Bakr (RA)
Keeping all the work in your own hands and trusting no one
Not letting any outsider into any step, out of fear

quiz.q: You work in an organisation where everyone thinks their own work small. In the light of the journey to the cave of Thawr, what would you say?
o: Counting only the work of the one who goes first as real
No one’s work is small; all work together makes a journey
Moving on, leaving out the one who is afraid
Who was in the cave is the greatest matter, the rest are secondary
quiz.e: ‘Ali (RA), Asma’ (RA), ‘Abdullah, ‘Amir, the guide; the role of all.

quiz.q: Seeing the spider’s web at the mouth of the cave, what did Quraysh decide?
o: Set fire to the cave so that whoever was inside would come out
Called Abu Bakr (RA) to find who was inside
Split into groups and spread out in all directions to search
Had anyone entered, the web would not have been there; so they moved away

quiz.q: Who said to whom in the cave of Thawr, ‘What do you think of two of whom the third is Allah’?
o: The Prophet ﷺ to Abu Bakr (RA)
Abu Bakr (RA) to the Prophet ﷺ
‘Ali (RA) to the Prophet ﷺ
‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr (RA) to Abu Bakr (RA)

quiz.q: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3652, what did Abu Bakr (RA) do on the road at noon?
o: Spread a bed in the shade of a rock, brought milk
Asked Suraqah for a paper of security, when he was on his horse
Seeing the spider’s web at the cave’s mouth, moved away
Cut a waistband and tied the mouth of the pouch

porbos.title: Suraqah on the Road • Waiting at the Harrah • At Quba • Suhayb’s Gold • Where the She-Camel Knelt • From the Day the Years Were Counted • The First Word • Our Home Today • Final Word

blocks.1: After three nights they set out on the road. By then Quraysh had already announced. For the Prophet {{1}} and for Abu Bakr (RA), for each a reward equal to the blood-money of one man; for whoever would kill or capture them. A greedy hunter followed, lured by that reward. Suraqah ibn Malik.{{2}}
blocks.2: Abu Bakr (RA) has also told of that moment.
blocks.4: We set out, and the people were searching for us. No one caught up with us except Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum, on his horse. I said, O Messenger of Allah, the pursuer has caught up with us. He said, do not grieve, Allah is with us.{{1}}
blocks.5: What happened, in his own words.
blocks.7: I could hear the recitation of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}; he did not look back, while Abu Bakr (RA) kept looking back. Then the front legs of my horse sank into the ground, up to the knees. I fell from the horse. I scolded it; it stood up, but could hardly get its legs out. When it stood upright, from the marks of its legs a column of dust, like smoke, rose into the sky.{{2}}
blocks.8: The horse was running toward the hunter; and the ground itself seized it. Suraqah threw the arrow-lots to see good and ill omen. The result he did not want came out. He threw again. Again the same. Then he called out asking for security. They stopped.
blocks.10: Then this belief arose in my heart: after the obstruction I met in reaching them, the matter of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} will surely prevail. I said to him, your people have announced a blood-money reward for you; and I told them the news of what people wanted to do with them. I offered them provisions and goods; they did not reduce anything of mine, nor asked anything of me, only said, keep our matter secret.{{2}}
blocks.11: He who came for the greed of a reward went away with a written paper of security in his hand.
blocks.13: One thing needs to be said from here. Most of the scenes in this part are at the end of hadith number 3906 of Sahih al-Bukhari. That part is the narration of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. He is a Tabi‘i; he told the events without naming any Companion. So that part is mursal. The main structure, however, is also in the sound narration of Anas (RA); the Ansar’s welcome at the Harrah, going around him bearing arms. The rest of the details have been taken as scenes.{{1}}
blocks.14: A caravan beside the road. A group of Muslim traders returning from Syria. Among them al-Zubayr (RA).
blocks.16: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} met al-Zubayr (RA) in a Muslim caravan, who were returning from trade in Syria. Al-Zubayr (RA) clothed the Messenger of Allah {{2}} and Abu Bakr (RA) in white garments.{{3}}
blocks.17: And one small matter of that road Anas (RA) has told. It is sound, from the mouth of a Companion.
blocks.19: The Prophet {{1}} was coming toward Madinah, with Abu Bakr (RA) riding behind him. Abu Bakr (RA) was elderly, a well-known face; and the Prophet {{2}} was young, unknown to people. Someone would meet Abu Bakr (RA) and say, O Abu Bakr, who is this man in front of you? He would say, this man guides me on the way. The listener would think he meant the road. In fact he meant the path of good.{{3}}
blocks.20: Not a lie. Not a hiding of a lie either. A word that is true, and at the same time leads the listener in another direction. Meanwhile in Madinah.
blocks.22: The Muslims in Madinah heard of the Messenger of Allah’s {{1}} leaving Makkah. Every morning they would go to the Harrah and wait for him, until the heat of noon sent them back. One day, after a long wait, they went back. When they had entered their houses, a Jew climbed up a high fortress of theirs for some purpose. He saw the Messenger of Allah {{2}} and his companions in white garments, the mirage moving away before them. He could not hold himself, and cried out at the top of his voice, O people of the Arabs, here is your good fortune that you were waiting for!{{3}}
blocks.23: Then what the Ansar did, in the words of Anas (RA),
blocks.25: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} alighted beside the Harrah, then sent for the Ansar. They came and greeted the two of them and said, mount, safe and obeyed. Then the Prophet {{2}} and Abu Bakr (RA) mounted, and the Ansar went around them with weapons in hand. In Madinah it was said, the Prophet of Allah has come, the Prophet of Allah has come!{{3}}
blocks.26: What they had promised on the night of ‘Aqabah, here they kept with their own hands.
blocks.28: Monday. The month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal. The Prophet {{1}} alighted in the upper part of the city, in the settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf; that is Quba.{{2}}
blocks.31: Abu Bakr (RA) stood before the people, and the Messenger of Allah {{1}} sat silent. The Ansar who had not seen the Messenger of Allah {{2}} before came and began greeting Abu Bakr (RA). At last the sun fell on the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Then Abu Bakr (RA) came forward and shaded him with his cloak. Only then did the people recognise the Messenger of Allah {{4}}.{{5}}
blocks.32: At Quba the Prophet {{1}} stayed fourteen nights.{{2}}
blocks.33: In these very days that mosque was founded whose foundation is on taqwa; the Prophet {{1}} prayed in it.{{2}}
blocks.34: ‘Ali (RA) arrived at Quba. Staying three more nights in Makkah he had returned, one by one, the trusts people had left with the Prophet {{1}}.{{2}}
blocks.35: At Quba he stayed near the house of a Muslim widow. At night he would see someone come and knock on her door, she comes out, the man leaves something. Suspicion arose in ‘Ali’s (RA) mind. He asked, servant of Allah, who is this who comes to your door every night? You are a Muslim woman, you have no husband. The woman said, this is Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA). He knows I have no one. When evening comes he breaks the idols of his tribe, brings the pieces to me. He says, use these as fuel. ‘Ali (RA) kept in mind this deed of Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA). After Sahl’s death, in Iraq, he himself told that story.{{1}}
blocks.37: While at Quba, one more arrived; leaving his gold. Suhayb (RA) had wanted to set out. Some youths of Quraysh stopped him. What happened then was in his own words.
blocks.39: I had intended to go out with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, but some youths of Quraysh stopped me. That night I kept standing up again and again, I did not sit. They said, Allah has kept him busy with his stomach. Yet I was not sick. They got up and left. I went out; after I had gone a ‘barid’, some of them caught up with me to bring me back. I said, do you want me to give you several uqiyyah of gold, and you leave my way and keep the promise made to me? They agreed. I went back with them to Makkah. I said, dig under the threshold of the door, there are uqiyyahs of gold; and go to such-and-such woman and take two sets of clothes. Then I set out and reached the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, before his moving away from Quba. Seeing me he said three times, O Abu Yahya, profitable was this trade! I said, O Messenger of Allah, no one came to you before me; no one informed you except Jibril (AS).{{3}}
blocks.40: He had bought the way with gold. And the word with which the Prophet {{1}} welcomed him is ‘profit’. What we count as loss, the Prophet {{2}} often calls profit.
blocks.42: After fourteen nights the Prophet {{1}} sent for Banu Najjar. That day Anas (RA) saw with his own eyes.
blocks.44: The Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah, and alighted in the upper part of the city in a settlement named Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. There he stayed fourteen nights. Then he sent for Banu Najjar. They came with swords hanging. It is as if I am still seeing it, the Prophet {{2}} on his mount, Abu Bakr (RA) behind him, and the men of Banu Najjar around him; in this way he came and halted in the courtyard of Abu Ayyub (RA).{{3}}
blocks.45: From Quba the Prophet {{1}} set out on Friday. In the valley of Banu Salim ibn ‘Awf the time of Jumu‘ah came. He prayed in the mosque there. That is the first Jumu‘ah in Madinah. Then tribe after tribe came to block the way. ‘Utban of Banu Salim and ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) said, O Messenger of Allah, stay with us. We have numbers, equipment, protection. The Prophet {{2}} said, ‘leave the she-camel’s way, she is commanded.’ Banu Bayadah came and said the same. The same reply. On behalf of Banu Sa‘idah, Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA). The same reply. On behalf of Banu al-Harith, Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA), Kharijah, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA). The same reply. Banu ‘Adi ibn Najjar, the tribe of his maternal uncles, said, your maternal uncles are here. The same reply.{{3}}
blocks.46: Every tribe wanted him to stay in their house. The Prophet {{1}} named no one. Wherever the she-camel goes. Exactly where the she-camel knelt, that account is in the narration of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. That part too is mursal.
blocks.48: Then he mounted his mount, and the people walked with him. At last the she-camel knelt at the place of the Messenger’s mosque in Madinah, where that day some Muslims were praying. The place was a date-drying yard of two orphan boys named Suhayl and Sahl, who were in the care of As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA). When the she-camel knelt with him, the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, God willing, this is the dwelling.{{2}}
blocks.50: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} called the two boys, wanting to bargain for the yard to build a mosque. They said, no, O Messenger of Allah, we give it to you as a gift.{{2}}
blocks.51: In the narration of Anas (RA), however, the mention of the land comes in the name of Banu Najjar.{{1}}
blocks.52: Then the mosque began to rise. The narration of Anas (RA),
blocks.54: He ordered the building of the mosque. Calling the men of Banu Najjar he said, O Banu Najjar, fix the price of this garden of yours. They said, no, by Allah, we ask its price from no one but Allah. In it were graves of the polytheists, some ruins and date palms. The Prophet {{1}} gave the order; the graves were dug up and removed, the ruins were levelled, the date palms were cut down. The cut trunks were placed in a row toward the mosque’s qiblah, and stones were set on both sides of the door. They recited rhythmic verses as they carried the stones, and the Prophet {{2}} was with them; he was saying, O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter; so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.{{3}}
blocks.55: He who once went from market to market saying, who will give me shelter, is now carrying stones with his own hands.
blocks.56: From the Day the Years Were Counted
blocks.57: From which day does the Muslim nation’s calendar begin? It could have begun from the day the Prophet {{1}} received revelation. It could have begun from the day he passed away. In the words of Sahl ibn Sa‘d (RA) the counting began from another day.{{2}}
blocks.59: They did not count (the years) from the day the Prophet {{1}} received prophethood, nor even from the day of his passing; they counted only from the day of his arrival in Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.61: What was the Prophet’s {{1}} first word on the soil of Madinah? ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) was in the crowd that day. He is a man of the lineage of Bani Isra’il.
blocks.63: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} came to Madinah, people rushed toward him; it was said, the Messenger of Allah {{2}} has come. I too went with the people to see him. When the face of the Messenger of Allah {{3}} became clear to me, I understood that this face is not the face of a liar.{{4}}
blocks.64: And what he said first of all,
blocks.66: The first thing he said was: O people, spread the salam, feed food, and pray when people are asleep; you will enter Paradise in peace.{{1}}
blocks.67: In the first sermon there is no talk of war, no talk of power.
blocks.69: This story returns to our home today at several places. The first place is that of trust and calculation. In the Hijrah, in each task of the Prophet {{1}} there was one person. A person to gather news at night. A person to graze goats. A person to show the road. A person to lie in the bed. Four months of feeding two camels. Both together. The student who without opening the book says, Allah is my trust; he is not speaking of trust, he is giving his laziness a beautiful name. And the businessman who calculates everything, and still cannot sleep at night from uncertainty, has put the calculation itself in the place of Allah. The Prophet {{2}} showed; first the hand moves, then trust. Trust is not the name of sitting with hands folded.
blocks.70: The second place is that of giving shelter. For ten years the Prophet {{1}} called, who will give me shelter? Today that call comes in another language. A plot of land for a mosque. A good teacher for a madrasah. The study expenses of an orphan. A corner to lay one’s head for a servant of the din. The Ansar responded. About them the Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.72: The sign of faith is love for the Ansar, and the sign of hypocrisy is hatred for the Ansar.{{1}}
blocks.73: To love and honour those who give shelter to the din is itself a sign of faith. The third place is the gold of Suhayb (RA). Such a time comes before us too. A road of haram income. A file of bribery. A usurious dealing, in which everything is in order, only Allah’s permission is missing.
blocks.74: The fourth place is that of telling openly. On the night of ‘Aqabah As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA) said, know the risk first, then stretch out the hand. No one kept anyone in the dark. Today when we call others to the path of the din, we do not tell of the hardship. We make a marriage proposal and hide the risk. We call someone to a task and conceal the possibility of loss. One who stretches out the hand knowingly does not easily let go. The men of the night of ‘Aqabah stretched out exactly that hand.
blocks.75: The fifth place is that of the teacher. To fill a city with faith, one teacher had gone that day, only the Qur’an in his hand. Today in our neighbourhood, with whom do the children learn the Qur’an? How much do we give the maktab teacher, how much do we keep track of?
blocks.76: The sixth place is the tug between home and din. Umm Salamah (RA) wept for a year sitting by the roadside. ‘Ayyash (RA) was turned back in the name of his mother’s oath. Even today our homes have their pull. The call of mother and father, the pressure of relatives, the fear of the home. Not every call is a trap; nor is every call sincere. The word of ‘Umar (RA) was simple; first know who is behind the call.
blocks.77: The seventh place is that of the unnamed people. ‘Ali (RA) lay in the bed. ‘Amir grazed the goats. ‘Abdullah brought news. Asma’ (RA) cut her waistband. ‘Ali (RA) stayed on in Makkah to return the trusts. Today in our mosques, madrasahs, institutions there are such people; they open the door, wash the plates, keep the news. How much do we remember their names?
blocks.78: The eighth place is that of small good. Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) once gave security to the merchants of Quraysh in his area. And the names of those two pulled him up from the roads of Makkah. People with whom today there is only dealing, tomorrow those very ones can come and stand by. No one knows whom and when a small good conduct will serve. There is also Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA). In the darkness of the night, informing no one, he used to leave fuel at a widow’s door. Which is our ‘secret’ good deed?
blocks.79: The ninth place is that of the first word. How much of these three is there in our homes today? The salam first to the neighbour. A plate to the hungry house next door. And rising from sleep for at least two rak‘ahs.
blocks.81: In today’s dars we heard the story of searching for a home. Ten years of going from market to market. The six of Yathrib. Then the twelve. The terms of the night of ‘Aqabah; and the hands of the seventy-three. Then the council of Makkah, that bed, the cave on Mount Thawr. Then Suraqah, the white clothes of al-Zubayr (RA), the sun of Quba, the halting of the she-camel.
blocks.82: At the beginning of the dars I put a question. Did the Prophet {{1}} only trust, or did he also calculate? The answer is at the mouth of the cave. The work we leave lying and sit still saying ‘Allah is my trust’, whether the calculation for that work was first made, that is today’s question of the dars. In the next dars we will see what the Prophet {{2}} first built in this new home.
blocks.83: So take one deed with you from today’s dars.
blocks.85: The Prophet {{1}} called for ten years in search of a home, then hid three nights in the cave, and calculated at every step; yet inside the cave he said, Allah is with us.
blocks.86: Today I will ask myself a question: for the work I have left lying saying ‘Allah is my trust’, what calculation have I made? Today I will write a plan for that work on paper, who will do it, what they will do, when they will do it; which I will not leave from today on.

quiz.q: After Suraqah fell from the horse, seeing what did the belief arise in his mind that the Prophet’s ﷺ cause will prevail?
o: Seeing the spider’s web, which was at the mouth of the cave; so it seemed
The horse’s legs sinking up to the knees
Seeing a force coming from the sky, mentioned in the verse; therefore
Seeing the Prophet’s ﷺ white garments, which al-Zubayr (RA) had put on him; therefore

quiz.q: You meet suddenly someone who had come to harm you. In the incident of Suraqah, what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
o: Took him prisoner at once and brought him to the cave
Sent him away with gold, as Suhayb (RA) had given
Gave a written paper of security, and said keep it hidden
Hid him in the cave and made him keep the matter secret

quiz.q: Why is the scene of waiting at the Harrah separately called ‘mursal’?
o: Ibn Hajar called the chain weak, so it is mursal
The narrator was a child at the time of the event, so it is mursal
‘Urwah is a Tabi‘i; he told the event without naming a Companion
The narration is in a book outside Sahih al-Bukhari, so it is mursal
quiz.e: Last part of Sahih al-Bukhari 3906; the main structure matches the narration of Anas (RA) (3911, 428).

quiz.q: Someone asked you who the companion is. What can be learned from Abu Bakr’s (RA) ‘this man guides me on the way’?
o: A lie can be told if the purpose is good, the dars says so
Staying silent at someone’s question is the only way, the dars says so
Always hiding the Prophet’s ﷺ identity is the only means
The word was true, the listener understood it in another sense
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3911 (Anas (RA)); the explanation is the narrator’s.

quiz.q: When Quraysh’s men caught Suhayb (RA) after he had set out, how did he get released?
o: By agreeing to give gold
By asking for a written paper of security like Suraqah
By lying in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed like ‘Ali (RA)
By weaving a spider’s web and covering the mouth of the cave

quiz.q: A man gave up an opportunity of haram income. With whose case in the dars does that match?
o: Suhayb’s (RA); he bought the way with gold
Suraqah’s; following for the greed of a reward, he went back when his horse sank
Abu al-Haytham’s; he asked a question before cutting the old pacts
Abu Ayyub’s (RA), near whose courtyard the she-camel came and halted

quiz.q: Land is needed to build a mosque in your neighbourhood. Which scene would inspire you most?
o: Suraqah falling from his horse when he came to catch, that itself
Abu Bakr (RA) shading the Prophet ﷺ with his cloak, in the sun at Quba, that itself
Asma’ (RA) cutting her waistband and tying the pouch, before the journey to the cave, that itself
Banu Najjar not asking a price and the Prophet ﷺ himself carrying stones

quiz.q: A new neighbour has come. In the light of the Prophet’s ﷺ first word in Madinah, what should be done?
o: Hold a secret meeting with him like at ‘Aqabah
First salam, food and night prayer
Write a paper of security like Suraqah
Call him quickly to faith like the six

quiz.q: A student goes into the exam without opening the book and says ‘Allah is my trust’. According to the dars, what is his statement?
o: Complete tawakkul like the cave of Thawr, where preparation came first
Asking for a promise of security like Suraqah, instead of trust
Not trust; giving his own laziness a beautiful name
Going ahead taking a risk like the night of ‘Aqabah, keeping trust

quiz.q: In the matter of love and honour for the helpers of a new religious project, which hadith does the dars recall?
o: The sign of faith is love for the Ansar
Prayer at its proper time is the most beloved deed
Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times more
The first reckoning is of prayer

quiz.q: You have left a task lying, saying ‘Allah is my trust’. What is the first step of the practical resolve?
o: Making a longer du‘a and sitting without calculation, thinking it trust
Asking oneself: what calculation have I made for this task?
Handing the task to someone else and becoming relaxed, thinking it trust
Forgetting the task and drowning in other work, thinking it trust
quiz.e: The ‘Final Word’ and ‘Practical Resolve’ of the dars.
